correctness.rationale: The classic bipartite equality gives Γ=n. Every displayed template has exactly n vertices and satisfies domination and a private-neighbor criterion. The new exhaustive 625-state automaton records those criteria using radius-two windows; exact f7=f9, f8=f10 identities yield a two-period induction on max-plus optimal-prefix weights. Enumerating all optimal prefixes at length seven and the finite 492-node/704-edge augmented state closure excludes any non-template accepted zero-excess word for all greater lengths. Direct vertex-level census n=2..10 and boundary template tests validate the local predicates. The general conclusion follows from finite-state induction, not bounded brute force.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of every maximum minimal dominating set in an infinite family, strengthening a recently resolved numerical parameter. It reveals a constant-size extremizer family, a parity-driven two-solution difference, and non-independent extremizers despite Γ=α. This configuration-level structure is not obtained by a textbook deduction of Γ=n.
